 Live Updated 7 minutes ago Mexico GP F1 LIVE, Leclerc leads Verstappen and Hamilton on Lap 9/71 in Formula 1 Race
 Follow F1 Mexico GP LIVE updates from the 2026 Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix, lap-by-lap leaderboard as Leclerc, Verstappen and Hamilton battle for P1.
 Coverage by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta Updated November 1, 2026, 8:17 pm GMT Lewis Hamilton celebrates pole position ahead of George Russell at the 2026 F1 Mexico City Grand Prix (Photo: VAVEL) ADVERTISEMENT
 Mexican GP . Follow VAVEL on Google Live Last update 20:17 GMT 20:17 GMT 7 minutes ago Lap 9/71: Charles Leclerc holds P1 ahead of Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton as DRS battles heat up
 Through Lap 9/71 at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc controls the race pace out front, keeping Red Bull rival Max Verstappen and seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton at bay while Kimi Antonelli and George Russell chase in P4 and P5.
 Live Top-10 Running Order (Lap 9/71): P1 Charles Leclerc · P2 Max Verstappen · P3 Lewis Hamilton · P4 Kimi Antonelli · P5 George Russell · P6 Lando Norris · P7 Arvid Lindblad · P8 Oscar Piastri · P9 Franco Colapinto · P10 Nico Hülkenberg .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 20:14 GMT 9 minutes ago Lap 7/71: Charles Leclerc dictates the early pace ahead of Max Verstappen
 Charles Leclerc continues to dictate the pace out front on the seventh lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix, keeping Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton at bay as tyre management comes into focus. Behind the leading trio, Kimi Antonelli holds fourth place ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris. Arvid Lindblad, Franco Colapinto, Oscar Piastri and Nico Hülkenberg round out the top ten as DRS battles intensify through the midfield.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 20:10 GMT 14 minutes ago Lap 4/71: Max Verstappen moves past Lewis Hamilton into second behind Leclerc
 Charles Leclerc holds the lead at the Mexico City Grand Prix as the field settles into an early rhythm on the fourth tour, with drivers carefully managing their tyres. Max Verstappen now runs in second place ahead of Lewis Hamilton, while Kimi Antonelli and George Russell complete the top five. Further back, Arvid Lindblad sits sixth ahead of Lando Norris, Franco Colapinto, Oscar Piastri and Nico Hülkenberg in the points.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 20:09 GMT 14 minutes ago Lap 4/71: Max Verstappen charges on mediums behind Charles Leclerc after frantic Turn 1 duel
 Drama straight from the 830-metre run down into Turn 1 at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez! Pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton locked up his front soft tyre under heavy braking and went wheel-to-wheel with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc , allowing Leclerc to seize the race lead while Max Verstappen capitalised on his medium-compound start from fifth to slice up into second ahead of Hamilton. Over team radio, Hamilton felt he was squeezed wide through the opening chicane while Isack Hadjar spun to the back of the pack behind pit-lane starter Liam Lawson.
 Championship Watch & Lap 4/71 Top 10: Title leader Kimi Antonelli runs a composed fourth on softs (needing ninth or higher to clinch the 2026 Drivers' World Championship today). Order: P1 Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) · P2 Max Verstappen (Red Bull) · P3 Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) · P4 Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) · P5 George Russell (Mercedes) · P6 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) · P7 Lando Norris (McLaren) · P8 Franco Colapinto (Alpine) · P9 Oscar Piastri (McLaren) · P10 Nico Hülkenberg (Audi).
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 20:05 GMT 19 minutes ago Lap 1/71: Charles Leclerc surges into the lead ahead of Lewis Hamilton at Turn 1
 Lights out at the Mexico City Grand Prix and Charles Leclerc surges to the front of the pack on the opening tour, leading Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen through the first sector on cold tyres. Kimi Antonelli slots into fourth ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris as the 71-lap contest gets underway. Arvid Lindblad, Pierre Gasly, Nico Hülkenberg, and Franco Colapinto round out the early top ten.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 19:32 GMT an hour ago Pit Lane Open: Cars Head to the Grid at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
 The pit lane has officially opened in Mexico City and all 22 cars are making their installation laps to form up on the starting grid ahead of the 71-lap Grand Prix. Pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and front-row partner George Russell (Mercedes) face an 811-metre run down to Turn 1 where the slipstream effect at 2,240m altitude makes the start critical.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 19:31 GMT an hour ago 830-Metre Tow to Turn 1: Can Hamilton Fend Off Russell, Leclerc & Verstappen?
 With F1 LIVE and Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) race action moments away at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix , Lewis Hamilton launches from pole in his Ferrari facing the longest run from the grid to the first braking zone on the F1 calendar at 830 metres . Cars hit 350 km/h (217 mph) in the thin air, handing George Russell (P2) , Charles Leclerc (P3) and Andrea Kimi Antonelli (P4) a massive slipstream tow down to the tight right-left-right Turn 1–2–3 kerbs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 19:31 GMT an hour ago Home Favourite Spotlight: Sergio Pérez and Cadillac's First Mexico City Grand Prix
 Following our F1 LIVE and Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) build-up at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix , more than 140,000 spectators packed into the Estadio GNP Seguros grandstands are roaring for home favourite Sergio Pérez as Cadillac contests its inaugural Mexico City Grand Prix. Pérez starts P20 ahead of team-mate Valtteri Bottas (P21, power-unit penalty) and disqualified Liam Lawson (P22) , aiming to capitalise on Safety Car windows and Turn 1 drama.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 19:00 GMT an hour ago British Contingent Watch: Lando Norris (P6), Arvid Lindblad (P8) & Oliver Bearman (P14)
 As our F1 LIVE and Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) coverage of the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix counts down to lights out, three more Britons beyond Hamilton and Russell on Row 1 are poised to shape tonight's Mexican Grand Prix : McLaren's Lando Norris (P6) shares Row 3 with five-time Mexico winner Max Verstappen (P5) , Racing Bulls teenager Arvid Lindblad lines up a superb P8 alongside Isack Hadjar, and Haas driver Oliver Bearman starts P14 on free tyre choice right behind Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 18:26 GMT 2 hours ago Pirelli 71-Lap Tyre Strategy & Cooling Demands at 2,240 Metres Altitude
 In our F1 LIVE and Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) technical build-up to the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix , racing at 2,240 metres (7,350 feet) above sea level cuts air density by roughly 22%, forcing engineers to bolt on Monaco-spec wing angles while generating less downforce than Monza. Carbon-fibre brake ducts and power-unit cooling louvres are opened to the limit across all 71 laps , with Pirelli projecting a Medium-to-Hard one-stop as the baseline tyre strategy unless front-left graining triggers a two-stop sprint.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:55 GMT 2 hours ago All-British Front Row: Hamilton's 105th Career Pole & Russell Just 0.009s Behind
 Lewis Hamilton produced a sensational 1:16.514 flyer in Q3 on Saturday to claim his 105th career Formula 1 pole position - his first in Scuderia Ferrari red and his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix. Former Mercedes team-mate George Russell missed out by a mere 0.009 seconds to seal an all-British front row, with Charles Leclerc (+0.119s) third.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:25 GMT 3 hours ago Official 2026 Mexican Grand Prix Starting Grid: All-British Front Row Leads 22-Car Field
 Following stewards' penalties for Max Verstappen (one-place FP2 grid drop), Valtteri Bottas (power-unit component penalties) and Liam Lawson (qualifying disqualification for an MGU-K electrical demand infringement), five British drivers feature inside the top 14 on the official 22-car starting grid for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix :
 Row 1 (All-British Lockout): 1. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) · 2. George Russell (Mercedes)
 Row 2: 3. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) · 4. Andrea Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)
 Row 3: 5. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) · 6. Lando Norris (McLaren)
 Row 4: 7. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) · 8. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)
 Row 5: 9. Pierre Gasly (Alpine) · 10. Nico Hülkenberg (Audi)
 Rows 6–11: 11. Franco Colapinto (Alpine) · 12. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) · 13. Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) · 14. Oliver Bearman (Haas) · 15. Carlos Sainz (Williams) · 16. Alexander Albon (Williams) · 17. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) · 18. Ryo Hirakawa (Haas) · 19. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin) · 20. Sergio Pérez (Cadillac) · 21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) · 22. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:00 GMT 3 hours ago 2026 F1 World Championship Standings Entering the Mexican Grand Prix
 Here is how the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Drivers' and Constructors' Championships stand ahead of lights out at 8:00 PM GMT, with British stars George Russell , Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris all firmly in the hunt behind runaway rookie leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli:
 Drivers' Top 7: 1. Andrea Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) – 365 pts · 2. George Russell (Mercedes) – 242 pts · 3. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) – 241 pts · 4. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) – 236 pts · 5. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) – 233 pts · 6. Lando Norris (McLaren) – 211 pts · 7. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) – 144 pts.
 Constructors' Top 5: 1. Mercedes (607 pts) · 2. Ferrari (474 pts) · 3. Red Bull Racing (355 pts) · 4. McLaren (355 pts) · 5. Racing Bulls (102 pts).
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:00 GMT 3 hours ago UK Start Time & TV Channel: How to Watch the 2026 F1 Mexico City Grand Prix Live
 Here are the official lights-out times, television channels and F1 LIVE / Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) streaming details for tonight's 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix (Mexican Grand Prix) :
 United Kingdom & Ireland: 8:00 PM GMT (build-up from 6:30 PM GMT) - Live on Sky Sports F1 , Sky Sports Main Event and streaming on NOW ; Channel 4 airs extended race highlights later tonight.
 United States & Canada: 3:00 PM EST / 12:00 PM PST - Live on Apple TV (US) and TSN / RDS (Canada).
 Mexico (Local Time): 2:00 PM CST - Live on Canal 5 , FOX Sports México and F1 TV Pro .
 Australia: 7:00 AM AEDT (Monday, 2 November) - Live on Fox Sports and Kayo Sports .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:00 GMT 3 hours ago Circuit Guide: High Kerbs, Thin Air & Estadio GNP Seguros at Hermanos Rodríguez
 Situated inside the Magdalena Mixhuca parkland in Mexico City at 2,240 metres above sea level , the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez measures 4.304 km (2.674 miles) across 17 corners. Scheduled for 71 laps (305.354 km) , the circuit pairs blistering carbon-fibre aero efficiency down its 1.2 km pit straight with heavy kerb-riding through the sweeping Esses and the atmospheric Estadio GNP Seguros (Foro Sol) stadium section in Sector 3.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 17:00 GMT 3 hours ago Welcome to VAVEL UK's Live Coverage of the 2026 F1 Mexican Grand Prix!
 Good evening and welcome to VAVEL UK's F1 LIVE and Formula 1 LIVE (Formula1) lap-by-lap coverage of the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix ! Lights out is set for 8:00 PM GMT as Britain's Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and George Russell (Mercedes) lock out the front row ahead of Charles Leclerc , Andrea Kimi Antonelli , Max Verstappen and Lando Norris . Stay right here for grid tyre choices, pit-stop strategy and real-time leaderboard updates across all 71 laps!
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 The 2026 Formula 1 World Championship stages its high-altitude showdown tonight, Sunday, 1 November 2026, at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez for the 71-lap Mexico City Grand Prix (Mexican Grand Prix) . Lights out is scheduled for 8:00 PM GMT in the UK (3:00 PM EST / 2:00 PM CST local) with live British television coverage on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event .
 Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton leads an all-British front-row lockout after snatching his 105th career F1 pole —and his first in Scuderia Ferrari colours—just 0.009 seconds ahead of Mercedes' George Russell , with Charles Leclerc (P3), championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli (P4), Max Verstappen (P5) and McLaren's Lando Norris (P6) right behind.

 Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta has been director of VAVEL's Colombia edition since 2018. He joined VAVEL in 2014 as a writer and worked as a coordinator before taking charge of the edition. Based in Medellín, he covers Colombian football — especially the Antioquia clubs and Independiente Medellín — as well as international and women's football, cycling and other sports, and has covered thousands of matches live for VAVEL's Colombia, Mexico and US editions. He is a systems engineer, trained as a television and media technician, and works as a communicator for Club Real Antioquia's youth teams.
